accuracy.evidence: Checked against Common Core ELA L.K.4b (use inflections and affixes such as -ed, -s, re-, un-, pre-, -ful, -less as a clue to meaning), L.1.4b and L.1.4c (affixes and roots), L.2.4b and c, and the National Curriculum in England English Appendix 1 Year 1 (-s, -es, -ing, -ed, -er, -est; un- changes the meaning of verbs and adjectives). The adult text separates agentive -er (verb to noun: painter, teacher) from comparative -er (adjective: taller), which is the linguistically correct reason the root decides the meaning, and every un- example is either not + adjective or reversal of a verb.

misconceptions.evidence: Each documented slip has its own check: un- read as very or again (step 2 tempting cards 'very happy', 'lock it again', mastery m6, challenge 'painted again' and 'painted a lot'), any final s read as plural (step 3 bus and dress panels, challenge bus vs pens, mastery m1), every -er read as more (step 4 sort, practice p5 'more farm', challenge 'more climb'), and the time clue in -ed missed (step 1, challenge 'He is rowing now' and 'He will row later').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagpeel is about reading parts for meaning, not spelling them: time sorting by the -ed clue, picking the meaning of un- words, matching word to a one-or-three picture with drawn balls, hats, cups, buses, bugs and dresses, sorting -er by the job of the root, and a three-slot builder where the child drags un to the front or -ed, -s, -er to the end of a root from a meaning clue. It differs from flagunpre (spelling un- words) and flagvend (spelling verb endings); lab_distinct stayed under 30% against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child meets each rule by acting on it: dropping kicks into Already happened returns 'kicks has no ed at the end. It is not over yet: it happens now'; tapping three cups for bus returns 'bus ends in s, but the s is part of the word. Take it off: bu is not a word'; a wrong build names the clue word that needed the part ('The clue says more than one. That needs s at the end'). Done screens list each word with its meaning so the pattern is visible.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions each hold a tempting wrong answer the step then disproves: that Sam is kicking the ball right now (step 1 shows -ed means it already happened), that unhappy means very happy (step 2 flips five words), and that er always means more (step 4 sorts painter, farmer, singer and teacher into the person room). The done line repeats the learner's prediction through A.reveal.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions with twelve distinct wrong-answer messages, each naming the slip: un as again, un as a lot, -ed as now, -ed as later, -er on a doing word read as more, the climber as the thing climbed, no s on pen, the s in bus as part of the word, unsoft for softer, softs for softer, unwrapped as more paper and unwrapped as never wrapped. The builder step adds six more messages naming the missing or extra part.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences and everyday words (Sam kicked the ball. That is over. He is not kicking it now.) and pass the family readability limit in validate_lessons. Canvas words are 26 to 30 px on white cards with one instruction per round; the young class gives large buttons. The adult text uses the precise terms morpheme, root, prefix, suffix, inflection, agentive and comparative -er with the standard codes.

no_filler.evidence: The content gate found no banned phrases and the explanation stayed under 12% six-word overlap with every lesson, including The Prefix un- and Spelling Verb Endings. Every feedback line names the word and the part that carries the clue; step texts are one rule and one example each.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px (Android-size viewport, touch) in light and dark for all six steps after Show me: the two sorting rooms wrap their labels onto two lines (It already / happened, A person who / does it), the one and three picture panels sit side by side, the front, root and end slots fit with the Check button below them and the four part tiles on one row at the bottom, and the button row wraps cleanly under the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: The browser gate completed every task with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13, the challenge showed, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) found no violations in light or dark. Every drag or tap has a labelled button ('jumped: It already happened', 'unhappy means not happy', 'balls: more than one', 'un at the front', 'Check the word'), and the canvas aria-label is rewritten with every feedback line. Canvas text is dark ink on pale cards in both themes; part tiles are #831843 on #fce7f3.
